reason: The cited evidence confirms that substrate heating is a known strategy to mitigate thermal stresses and cracking in AM (E2), and that in situ thermal management can reduce cooling rates and cracking (E3), but none of the passages provide specific data on AlCrFeNiSi, the 300–350 °C range, or the claimed quantitative outcomes (~10–15% yield strength increase, ~20% residual stress reduction). E1 discusses post-process heat treatment, not in situ preheating, and is only loosely related. Thus, the general mechanism is supported, but the material-specific and quantitative premises lack direct eviden
premises: Substrate preheating to 300–350 °C reduces thermal gradients in LPBF
Reduced thermal gradients lower residual stresses and compositional segregation
Lower residual stress and segregation enhance mechanical integrity (yield strength, defect density)
These effects apply specifically to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder in LPBF
The benefits are achievable without altering other standard AM process parameters
